actions.summary: Blocked ChatGPT on school-issued devices and the district network for students, citing the new 20-person group-chat feature and planned adult content as things that could facilitate harmful interaction or content about self-harm, violence and bullying. Google Gemini and MagicSchool stayed available.
actions.notes: Announced by CIO Richard Charles in a 2026-01-10 email to families, effective the following week. A district AI committee was to consider extending the block to staff. Colorado's largest district; the first big-district ChatGPT block of 2026.

actions.summary: Gave students monitored access to Gemini, NotebookLM and MagicSchool - the approved-platform side of the same posture that blocks ChatGPT.
actions.notes: Reported as 'last spring' in an Axios roundup dated 2026-08-13; effective_from is approximate. Paired with the January ChatGPT block above, which is why Colorado reads as mixed rather than restrictive.

actions.summary: Blocks district AI access outright for K-8 students and allows only approved Google tools in high school; the district's AI task force is being replaced by a standing steering committee to keep the guidelines current.
actions.notes: Included as the first K-8 AI block by a Colorado district, not on size. Single source (Axios local, 2026-08-13) which describes the posture heading into 2026-27 rather than a dated board vote; effective_from is the reporting date. Worth a second source. K-8 blocked entirely; 9-12 limited to approved Google tools.

actions.summary: Going the other way from its neighbors: rolling AI in, with Gemini certification offered to older students and staff by 2027 and K-5 digital-citizenship lessons underneath it.
actions.notes: Colorado's third-largest district. Single source (Axios local, 2026-08-13), describing the 2026-27 posture rather than a dated vote; effective_from is the reporting date. Cherry Creek's 'safe, smart, social' guidelines are in the same article and are a candidate row if a primary source turns up.
